title: What a Phone Repair Shop Can See, and How to Protect Your Data
html:
A technician who has your unlocked phone can see what is on it. So before repair, back up, then use the phone's built-in repair protection if it has one: Repair mode on Pixel phones, Maintenance mode on Samsung Galaxy phones. Other brands have different options or none. If your phone has no such mode, back up, remove what you can, and ask the shop what it will do.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

I looked for Repair mode or Maintenance mode on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14) on 11 Oct 2026 and did not find it, so I could not try it on this phone.

1. Back up first

Both Google and Samsung strongly recommend a backup before repair. Google says to back up your data before every repair service. Samsung says to back up before using Maintenance mode, in case the phone needs a factory reset or the storage is replaced during the repair. Parts replacement that affects storage may require data deletion even if you used the repair mode.

2. Pixel: Repair mode

Go to Settings, then System, then Repair mode, follow the steps and enter your PIN, password or pattern. Google says Repair mode starts a clean Android OS in a dedicated secure partition with limited functions. Technicians can use certain default first-party apps for diagnostics, but cannot access your personal data. It needs Android 14 (the December 2023 update or later) and 2 GB of free space. Do not create a new PIN while in Repair mode, and remember that changes made in it are not saved when you exit. To exit, return to the same screen, confirm with your lock, and let the phone restart.

3. Samsung: Maintenance mode

Go to Settings, then Device care, then Maintenance mode, and turn it on. Samsung says Maintenance mode creates a separate user account and hides your personal data, such as photos, videos, contacts and messages. The technician uses that separate account. To exit, tap the Maintenance mode notification and choose Exit, or go back to Device care, Maintenance mode, Exit. You need your lock code.

4. Other brands

We have not confirmed that Xiaomi, Redmi, realme, Oppo, vivo or OnePlus phones have a similar mode. Check your maker's support page for "repair mode" or "service mode" for your model.

On my vivo V23 Pro (Funtouch OS 14), Settings, then System lists System navigation, Global search, Languages and input, Date and time, Backup and restore, Reset options, Multiple users, Device clone and Developer options. I did not see a Repair mode or Maintenance mode there. Reset options has four entries: Reset Wi-Fi, mobile and Bluetooth, Reset app preferences, Reset all settings, and Erase all data (factory reset). I did not tap any of them. Multiple users is on the same System screen. I did not test a repair or service mode on any other phone.

5. If your phone has no repair mode

  • Back up, then remove or sign out of accounts you can do without for a few days, such as email, banking and UPI apps.
  • Turn off biometrics and use a temporary PIN you will change afterwards.
  • Do not hand over your Google account password or a one-time code. Ask the shop why it needs them if it asks.
  • Note your IMEI and take photos of the phone's condition before you leave it.
  • Ask the shop: will anyone need to unlock the phone, what will be tested, and what happens to the old parts?

6. After the repair

Check your accounts and settings. If your Google account was signed out or you shared a PIN, change it: Google account checklist. If you see unexpected sign-ins, apps you do not recognise or one-time codes you did not ask for, see how to check your phone.

What to do next

  1. Back up your phone.
  2. Turn on Repair mode or Maintenance mode if you have it.
  3. Ask the shop what it will do, and check the phone after the repair.
